reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g1_mg_q1_0), 2026-08-19

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample set directly addresses the learning competency requiring students to identify simple 2D shapes (triangle, rectangle, square) under different sizes and orientations. Triangle identification is tested in real-world and geometric contexts such as "A party hat is shaped with 3 straight edges. What 2D shape is it?" and "A small flat shape with 3 straight edges is shown. What shape is it?". Rectangle identification is tested in "A classroom chalkboard has 4 straight edges and opposite edges are equal. What shape is the chalkboard?", and square identification in "A large flat shape with 4 equal straight edges is shown. What shape is it?" and "A flat floor tile has 4 equal straight edges. What shape is the tile?". Orientation changes are specifically evaluated with "A small triangular sign is turned upside down. What shape is it?".

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All specified 2D shapes in the competency text (triangles, rectangles, and squares) are covered across the sample set. Size variations are represented ("A small flat shape with 3 straight edges is shown. What shape is it?" vs "A large flat shape with 4 equal straight edges is shown. What shape is it?") and orientation variation is represented ("A small triangular sign is turned upside down. What shape is it?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The sentence structures, vocabulary, and conceptual load are entirely developmentally appropriate for Grade 1 Quarter 1 students. Questions use familiar concrete objects and clear edge-based descriptions, e.g., "A party hat is shaped with 3 straight edges. What 2D shape is it?" and "A flat floor tile has 4 equal straight edges. What shape is the tile?", avoiding complex geometric language.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample demonstrates good structural diversity, incorporating real-world item contexts ("A classroom chalkboard has 4 straight edges and opposite edges are equal. What shape is the chalkboard?"), direct attribute descriptions ("A small flat shape with 3 straight edges is shown. What shape is it?"), size contrasts ("A large flat shape with 4 equal straight edges is shown. What shape is it?"), and spatial reorientation ("A small triangular sign is turned upside down. What shape is it?"), presented across mcq and read_mcq formats.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every item strictly adheres to the scope of identifying 2D simple shapes without leaking into 3D shapes or introducing higher-grade concepts like angle measures, perimeter calculations, or polygon classification outside the target domain. For instance, "A classroom chalkboard has 4 straight edges and opposite edges are equal. What shape is the chalkboard?" stays focused on distinguishing rectangles by opposite equal sides.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Number values and attribute counts are limited to 3 and 4 straight edges (e.g., "A small flat shape with 3 straight edges is shown. What shape is it?" and "A flat floor tile has 4 equal straight edges. What shape is the tile?"), which is precisely calibrated to early Grade 1 polygon recognition.
